title: U.S. House · Maryland's 2nd District
area: Much of Baltimore County and Carroll County, along with parts of Baltimore City.

context.text: Incumbent John Olszewski Jr. defeated Clint Spellman Jr. in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary. Dave Wallace defeated Nnabu Eze in the Republican primary; former candidate Kim Klacik did not make the ballot.

sources.title: United States House of Representatives elections in Maryland, 2026

summary.text: John Olszewski Jr. is the Democratic incumbent in Maryland's 2nd Congressional District. He previously served as Baltimore County Executive and in the Maryland House of Delegates.

background.text: Born in Baltimore, Maryland, in 1982; earned a bachelor's degree from Goucher College, a master's from George Washington University, and a Ph.D. in public policy from the University of Maryland-Baltimore County.
Worked as a Baltimore County public school teacher before serving over nine years in the Maryland House of Delegates.
Elected Baltimore County Executive twice, leading a $5 billion budget and more than 9,000 employees.

priorities.text: Expanding workforce development and enhancing education and housing access.
Defending the foundations of American democracy.

record.text: As a member of the Maryland House of Delegates, championed earned sick leave legislation and a minimum wage increase.
Cast a vote in the Maryland Senate delegation vote that secured marriage equality in Maryland.

As Baltimore County Executive, launched a near-universal free community college program for county residents and created the county's first public campaign finance system and Office of the Inspector General.
Serves on the House Small Business Committee and House Foreign Affairs Committee for the 2025-2026 term.

summary.text: Dave Wallace is the Republican nominee for Maryland's 2nd Congressional District. He owns a kitchen wholesale business and has run for this seat in previous cycles.

background.text: Graduated from South Carroll High School and earned a B.S. in biology from Salisbury University.
Worked in immunological cancer research at the National Institutes of Health before founding Chesapeake Kitchen Wholesalers in 1981.
Founded the organization Restore America's Mission in 2008.

priorities.text: Protecting medical freedom, including the right to choose whether to wear a mask or take COVID vaccines.
Fighting government corruption, including support for term limits and a presidential line-item budget veto.
Protecting police and other first responders with resources and equipment.

positions.summary: Says he will vote to give police and other first responders the resources and equipment they need.
